design_note: Visualizes the chapter's two-part refund evaluation gate at adjacent success counts. A passing point estimate can still miss the lower-bound requirement; meeting both leaves hard authority and accounting gates intact.

source.title: 7.2.4.1. Confidence intervals
source.concept: Wilson intervals estimate uncertainty for a binary proportion using the observed count and sample size. The lower endpoint differs from the observed success rate.
source.scope: Original 120-case hypothetical outcomes and curriculum gate. Counts are constructed; this chart is neither a production result nor a safety certificate.

lesson.title: Ninety percent alone misses the refund gate
lesson.intro: Track A requires observed conversation success of at least 90% and a two-sided 95% Wilson lower bound of at least 85%. Compare four alternative constructed results for 120 independent cases.

data.method: Constructed counts; k = successful conversations. Two-sided Wilson, z = 1.96.

read: All four point estimates reach the separate 90% requirement.
The 85% line tests the lower endpoint, not the point estimate.
Only 110 and 111 successes put that lower endpoint above 85%.
lesson.question: Does 109 successful conversations pass both statistical requirements, and would 110 override an unauthorized refund?
lesson.answer: 109 / 120 is about 90.83%, but its Wilson lower bound is about 84.33%, so it fails the lower-bound requirement. At 110 successes the lower bound is about 85.34%, clearing these statistical gates. Any unauthorized refund still fails its independent hard gate; an aggregate quality score cannot erase it.
lesson.takeaway: Check the point estimate and uncertainty requirement separately, then apply every hard safety gate.
lesson.assumption: Constructed independent binary cases from one fixed hypothetical population; one fixed analysis. Alternative rows are not repeated peeks during a sequential test.
